title: ‘Monsters of God’ Finale Twist: The Final Boss and Rogue Special Agent
description: The finale of “Monsters of God,” a five-part docuseries from “Tiger King” creator Eric Goode exploring the exotic reptile smuggling trade, is an eye
body:
The finale of “Monsters of God,” a five-part docuseries from “Tiger King” creator Eric Goode exploring the exotic reptile smuggling trade, is an eye-opener.

	After exploring all avenues of the shady underworld of reptile smuggling, from reptile dealers and collectors to the zoos and the feds, the fifth part of the enthralling show — airing the night of Sept. 3 on HBO — sees Goode track down Anson Wong, a man known as the “Pablo Escobar of animal trafficking” who runs a vast network of wildlife smuggling operations out of Malaysia, capitalizing on the country’s lax wildlife protection laws and officials open to bribery. Goode sits down for an interview with Wong at his fortress in the mountains of Penang, and the two engage in a chummy discussion about his illegal empire.
	

	“I was definitely fearful the day before meeting him and wondering how this was going to play out,” Goode told Variety, adding, “Sometimes I wonder if I’m just being stupid. It’s not that I’m brave by any stretch, but you just feel it out. I don’t know if it’s the most nervous I’ve been, but it’s certainly up there.”




	But that isn’t the biggest surprise.

	During its final scenes, “Monsters of God” reveals that Ken McCloud, a special agent for the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service who worked tirelessly to apprehend Wong, has been keeping a ploughshare tortoise — the most endangered tortoise in the world, with only around 100 remaining in the wild — in his home.

	“Monsters of God” shows Goode entering McCloud and his wife Rose’s home with a hidden camera and capturing the ploughshare tortoise in a grubby terrarium in their living room. Goode had photographed McCloud and his wife years ago for a magazine, and says he got “upset” when the photo was published.
	

	“I didn’t know he was trying to keep it a secret,” Goode says. “He was very paranoid about theft, and didn’t even want to put the tortoise outside in his backyard because he was so worried that someone might steal it, since it’s so valuable. He got increasingly paranoid and that tortoise became more and more important to him, almost like his only child.”



	

					A ploughshare tortoise in “Monsters of God.”
									HBO
	



	Goode opted to use a hidden camera for the show because McCloud had grown so protective over the ploughshare tortoise that the last time he visited his home, the former special agent came out waving a gun.

	“It’s sad,” Goode says. “I asked him, ‘What separates the prisoner from the prison guard?’ and about the ethics of keeping that animal in solitary confinement by itself, and tried to convince him that that wasn’t the best place for that tortoise.”

	And then there’s the legal element. “I would think that the government would want to do something about it. If you were an ex-DEA agent who had a garage full of cocaine after you retired, you might think, ‘Hey, we’ve gotta do something about this ex-DEA agent!!’” adds Goode. “I’m still talking to people in the government about what to do about that.”



	

					Ken McCloud in “Monsters of God”
									HBO
	



	This is a personal issue for Goode, who is one of the world’s leading turtle conservationist. His nonprofit, the Turtle Conservancy, has helped protect 65 turtle species and preserved over 70,000 acres of wildlife across the world, and he is the U.S. Studbook Keeper for all American zoos on ploughshare tortoises, meaning it’s his job to keep track of all the ploughshare tortoises that aren’t in their native Madagascar. It’s his hope that the tortoise McCloud has stolen away will be placed in a breeding colony so that it can help grow the species. It’s also a lesson that even those on the side of the law can have unclean hands.

	“[McCloud’s] story is he used to work for a reptile dealer in L.A., so he just so happened to end up on the other side of the fence in law enforcement, but he could have ended up on a different side of the fence,” Goode says. “He has the fever, or the addiction, if you want to use a drug analogy, so he knew that he wanted those animals. And even though he was taking them from people that brought them in, he loved that he got to be the guy who kept them. It’s like the DEA agent who becomes an addict. There’s some weird psychological stuff going on there.”

schema.headline: ‘Monsters of God’ Finale Twist: The Final Boss and Rogue Special Agent

title: ‘Modern Family’ Duo Sets New Comedy Series ‘Mammoth’ on Fox
description:
A new live-action comedy series is heading to Fox.

	From “Modern Family” co-creator Christopher Lloyd and executive producer and writer Danny Zuker
body:
A new live-action comedy series is heading to Fox.

	From “Modern Family” co-creator Christopher Lloyd and executive producer and writer Danny Zuker comes “Mammoth,” which is based on Mike Bubbins’ British sitcom of the same name.

	Per the description, “‘Mammoth’ follows Coach Tony Mammoth, a larger-than-life high school gym teacher whose life is put on ice in 1983, when he’s buried in a freak ski avalanche. Forty years later, he thaws out to a world that has completely changed … but he’s convinced it really didn’t need to. Still clinging to life in the ‘80s – complete with his Burt Reynolds moustache and treasured Trans-AM –- Mammoth returns to the job he loves, only to discover that today’s rules, relationships, and realities bear little resemblance to the world he once knew.” 
	

	The show is slated to debut on Fox during the 2027-2028 season. It marks the network’s first live-action comedy series greenlight in more than two years.


	“Mammoth” is produced by Fox Entertainment Studios, with Lloyd and Zuker serving as writers, showrunners and executive producers. Mark Linsey and Angie Stephenson of BBC Studios Los Angeles, as well as Bubbins, are also EPs.

	“Tony Mammoth genuinely believes he mastered manhood the first time around, making his new reality the ultimate wakeup call and greatest challenge in an otherwise flawless life,” said Christopher Lloyd. “He’s charming, wildly self-assured, hopelessly out of step and, despite his many blind spots, impossible not to root for.” 

	Danny Zuker added, “Tony gets the second chance so many people wish for, only to find that his bravado doesn’t quite match his new reality. We love his shameless confidence, his fascination with a world he barely recognizes, and the big heart underneath it all. He’s a lot. We can’t wait to bring him to Fox.”

schema.headline: ‘Modern Family’ Duo Sets New Comedy Series ‘Mammoth’ on Fox

title: ‘Marriagetoxin’ Creators Joumyaku and Yoda Mizuki Tease Season 2: ‘There Is Plenty of Cool Action We Want You to See’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
A master assassin’s toughest job isn’t a kill order. It’s finding a wife. 

	That premise carried “Marriagetoxin” from a running Shonen Jump+ series
body:
A master assassin’s toughest job isn’t a kill order. It’s finding a wife. 

	That premise carried “Marriagetoxin” from a running Shonen Jump+ series into one of the standout anime of Spring 2026, and creators Joumyaku and Yoda Mizuki are already looking toward a second season set for January 2027.

	The series follows Hikaru Gero, a master assassin whose latest assignment is to secure an heir by finding a wife. The target of his most recent job, a marriage swindler named Mei Kinosaki, ends up joining him for that mission instead. Serialized on Shueisha’s Shonen Jump+, “Marriagetoxin” has surpassed one million copies in circulation worldwide, and its anime adaptation, directed by Hori Motonobu, is streaming on Crunchyroll ahead of a second season premiering in January 2027.
	

	On how the manga came together, Joumyaku says, “It started with the single idea of ‘a Poison Master goes on a search for marriage,’ and from there, as we built the characters and the story, everything I had read, experienced, and picked up along the way got layered onto it.”


	The audience reaction has exceeded what either creator anticipated. Joumyaku points to Kinosaki’s reception specifically, crediting the anime staff for carrying Yoda’s character designs and action work faithfully into the adaptation. Yoda says they are grateful to the readers who have supported the series, to everyone involved in making it, and to Joumyaku for teaming up with them. “What surprises me most is that so many readers have enjoyed it – enough that Volume 1 went straight into a reprint and the dream of an adaptation came true.” Yoda says.
	

	Both creators are already looking ahead to the second season. Joumyaku promises that even more captivating heroines will appear one after another, deepening the relationships surrounding Gero. “There is plenty of cool action we want you to see,” Joumyaku says, adding that they are very much looking forward to delivering it to fans. Yoda echoes that heading into Season 2, captivating new heroines arrive along with several characters they are fond of themselves.

	Because the story operates within the shonen framework even though most of its cast are adults, Joumyaku says the protagonist’s growth remains the story’s central axis, which is why depicting relationships and identity carries so much weight for the work. Yoda, who illustrates the manga, says the story itself is built by Joumyaku and the series editor rather than by them, but that the emotions are already fully expressed at the storyboard stage. For an artist who wants to depict emotion richly above all, they call it a genuinely enjoyable story to illustrate.

	That approach has extended to how the series treats gender presentation, an element fans and critics have singled out as unusually progressive for the genre. Joumyaku describes the subversive elements as something that emerged naturally rather than as a plan set from the outset, with the protagonist caught between family expectations and the pull to live authentically. “I have a rough picture of where things go through the final chapter, but it feels like we are building the story while working out together how the protagonist comes to terms with it all,” Joumyaku says.

	Asked about designing Kinosaki, Yoda says, “I had been told in advance that this character would appear in both traditionally masculine and feminine clothing, so on the art side, I designed Kinosaki so that the character holds up in either presentation.”

	Working with Hori, whose credits include “Metallic Rouge” and “Carole & Tuesday,” has also shaped the manga going forward. Joumyaku says ideas raised in the anime’s script meetings have fed back into key parts of the source material, pointing to the fully realized car-splitting sequence in Episode One as an example of the level of craft involved. They single out a scene from Chapter 12 of Volume Two, in which Ureshino dumps yakisoba on her head, as the one that stayed with them most, noting that it was given what they call a proper through-line in Part B of Episode Four. “It was amazingly good,” Joumyaku says.
	

	Yoda says the anime’s action choreography went well beyond anything scripted in the manga panels. Of watching it unfold, they say, “so this is how they were moving all along.” They add that seeing the anime’s rendering of Kinosaki’s eyes pushed them to draw the character bigger and cuter in the source material going forward.

	Looking toward the manga’s climax, Joumyaku says the urge to give everything to the story’s endpoint grows stronger by the day, while Yoda says they never expected their own dream of seeing their character designs made into figures to actually come true, and that going forward they want to draw even better character designs and illustrations, ones that also get made into figures.

schema.headline: ‘Marriagetoxin’ Creators Joumyaku and Yoda Mizuki Tease Season 2: ‘There Is Plenty of Cool Action We Want You to See’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Beyoncé Releases ‘B’Day 20th Anniversary Deluxe Edition’ Featuring Unreleased Songs, Collaborations With Selena and Maluma
description: To commemorate the 20th anniversary of her sophomore album, Beyoncé has released a remastered version of “B’Day” featuring Spanish recordings, previ
body:
To commemorate the 20th anniversary of her sophomore album, Beyoncé has released a remastered version of “B’Day” featuring Spanish recordings, previously released bonus tracks, and a few unheard songs including “Can I Watch You” featuring Pharrell and a new Spanish version of “Irreplaceable” featuring previously released vocals from the late Selena Quintanilla.

	In a press release shared with Variety, Beyoncé reflected on the 20-year milestone of the album, which was originally released on September 4, 2006. “I wanted the album to be big, percussive, hard, up-tempo, and energized, and it was important to me that we used live instrumentation,” she said. “Hip-hop was taking over at the time, but I was fighting to preserve the bridges, melodies, and harmonies that have always been at the heart of R&B. The goal was to blend those two worlds through the art of sampling. I loved the minimalism of a beautiful vocal arrangement over a simple drum loop or a classic guitar like ‘Irreplaceable’…but only if that 808 was banging underneath.”
	

	For the reissue, Beyoncé remastered the songs and videos, which were recolored and finished in 4k. The revamped visual for “Déjà Vu” featuring Jay-Z was also released alongside the album.

	“B’Day 20th Anniversary Deluxe Edition” features a handful of unheard tracks, including “Cuerpo Tumbao (Get Me Bodied)” with Maluma, marking her first collaboration with the Colombian artist. The release notes that the song samples Celia Cruz’s “La Negra Tiene Tumbao” and that Beyoncé has “long admired Cruz’s pride in her African culture.” The song was produced by Beyoncé, Edgar Barrera, Casta and co-produced by Ali “Ali Ali” Alvarez.
	

	Additionally, the reissue includes “Irreemplazable (Como La Flor)” featuring Selena Quintanilla, whose estate approved the duet. The release notes that Beyoncé “revered Selena,” a fellow Texan, “and remembers listening to her on the radio in Houston,” crediting the late singer for inspiring the recording of her 2007 Spanish EP “Irreemplazable.”

	“B’Day 20th Anniversary Edition” also includes new and rare tracks including “Morning Dew (Donk),” “Can I Watch You” (produced by Beyoncé and Pharrell), “My First Time,” “Lost Yo Mind,” “Creole” and “Back Up.

title: Leslie Odom, Jr. and Aunjanue Ellis-Taylor Join Storm Reid in Teyana Taylor’s Directorial Debut ‘Get Lite’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Golden Globe winner and Oscar and Grammy nominee Teyana Taylor is assembling an all-star cast for her feature directorial debut, “Get Lite,” starrin
body:
Golden Globe winner and Oscar and Grammy nominee Teyana Taylor is assembling an all-star cast for her feature directorial debut, “Get Lite,” starring Storm Reid and NFL rookie-turned-actor Ceyair Wright.

	Tony winner and Oscar nominee Leslie Odom, Jr. (“Hamilton,” “One Night in Miami”) and Oscar nominee Aunjanue Ellis-Taylor (“King Richard,” “Lucky”) have joined the ensemble cast for the Paramount movie, which follows a talented but sheltered dance student who finds inspiration, love and family in the last place he expected: the subways of New York City. Wright (“Space Jam: A New Legacy”) is the student caught between worlds, while Reid (“The Last of Us,” “Euphoria”) is the girl who opens his life to new possibilities. Key to the dance movie is Litefeet, a high-energy style that originated in Taylor’s hometown of Harlem.
	

	Production on “Get Lite” is set to begin this month in New York City; the film is dated for a wide theatrical release on Aug. 20, 2027. Taylor — who is coming off her acclaimed performance in “One Battle After Another” — directs from a screenplay by Maurice Williams, based on a spec script by Eric Gross that appeared on the Black List in 2020.


	Indie hip-hop artist Khayr Bullock, Twitch streamer Tylil James and actor Woody McClain (“Power Book II: Ghost,” “The Harder They Fall”) are also confirmed to join the cast. Jodie Turner-Smith (“Queen & Slim,” “The Agency”) and Asante Blackk (“When They See Us,” “This Is Us”) are in negotiations for key roles. 

	In addition to starring in the film, Reid is on board to produce alongside Kenya Barris and Anni Weisband for Barris’ Khalabo Ink Society; Robyn Simpson for A Seed & Wings Productions, Reid’s banner; and Bill Karesh for Offbrnd. Taylor is also producing the film with Courtney “Coco” Gilbert, under their production banner The Aunties.
	

	Taylor is represented by WME, Taylor Made Management and the Lede Company. CAA represents Reid, Odom, Jr. and Ellis-Taylor. Reid is also repped by the Lede Company and Granderson Des Rochers; Odom, Jr. by Untitled Entertainment and Jackoway Austen; and Ellis-Taylor by TMT Entertainment Group.

	McClain is represented by Buchwald, M88, Align PR and Goodman, Genow, Schenkman, Smelkinson & Christopher; Turner-Smith is represented by UTA, the Lede Company, 111 Media and Johnson Shapiro Slewett & Kole; and Blackk is represented by Gersh, 1v1 Entertainment, the Lede Company and Del Shaw Moonves.



	

					Ceyair Wright, Woody McClain, Jodie Turner-Smith and Asante Blackk.
									Blackk: Craig Mulcahy / Wright, McCain and Turner-Smith: Getty Images

title: Shakira, Romeo Santos, Prince Royce Among Top Winners at Premios Juventud 2026
description: Shakira, Prince Royce and Romeo Santos were among the top winners at Premios Juventud 2026, broadcast live from the Starlight Amphitheater in Marbel
body:
Shakira, Prince Royce and Romeo Santos were among the top winners at Premios Juventud 2026, broadcast live from the Starlight Amphitheater in Marbella, Spain on Thursday night.

	Royce and Santos shared three wins on the back of their collaborative project “Better Late Than Never,” which picked up best tropical album. Their tracks “Dardos” and “Lokita Por Mí” won tropical hit and tropical mix, respectively. Shakira, meanwhile, was named Premios Juventad female artist and won OMG collaboration for “Dai Dai” with Burna Boy as well as best pop song for “Bésame” with Alejandro Sanz. Aitana and Alejandro Fernández also received three awards.
	

	Elsewhere, Bad Bunny and Karol G won two awards apiece, as did Bizarrap, Carín León, Ovy on the Drums, Santos Bravos, Grupo Frontera, Beéle and Angelique Boyer.


	The award show, which was the culmination of a week of events in various cities across the globe, also bestowed the Agent of Change award upon Antonio Banderas, Marc Anthony, Yandel and La Oreja de Van Gogh. Jesús Vázquez hosted alongside Alejandra Espinoza and Clarissa Molina for the event, which was held in Europe for the first time this year.

title: Pablo Torre Sounds Off on the NBA’s Historic Ruling Against the Clippers, Kawhi Leonard and ESPN — and Teases His Next Big Sports Investigation
description:
Pablo Torre is feeling vindicated — sort of.

	Back in July, Variety spoke with the trailblazing sports journalist about “Pablo Torre Finds Out,” hi
body:
Pablo Torre is feeling vindicated — sort of.

	Back in July, Variety spoke with the trailblazing sports journalist about “Pablo Torre Finds Out,” his engrossing podcast, a mélange of chat show and true-crime docuseries wherein Torre breadcrumbs investigative reporting to his pals, and its monthslong, Pulitzer Prize-winning investigation into how the Los Angeles Clippers were alleged to have circumvented the NBA salary cap by having its star player, Kawhi Leonard, receive a $28 no-show endorsement deal from Aspiration, whose co-founder was recently sentenced to 14 years in prison for defrauding investors (Clippers owner Steve Ballmer, the richest owner in the league, among them).
	

	Ballmer had repeatedly — and vehemently — denied any involvement in the salary cap-circumvention scheme, and Torre had received a barrage of public criticism for his in-depth reporting from the likes of Ballmer’s billionaire pal (and former NBA owner) Mark Cuban and former NBA player turned podcaster Ty Lawson. His reporting was even undermined by his former employer, ESPN, in an Aug. 17 story by reporters Don Van Natta Jr., Baxter Holmes and Ramona Shelburne, under the headline, “Sources: NBA has no evidence Ballmer funneled money to Leonard via sponsors,” and the news site Puck, whose writers Dylan Byers and Peter Hamby accused Torre of chasing “clout and clicks and building your audience.”  


	But on Sept. 2, the NBA handed down its punishment, and it was historic (translation: the biggest penalty levied against a team in league history):


The Clippers will lose five first-round picks, in 2029, 2030, 2031, 2032 and 2033.
The Clippers will be fined $30 million.
Clippers owner Steve Ballmer will be suspended for one year “for knowingly seeking to help Mr. Leonard obtain off-court income opportunities.”
Leonard’s uncle, Dennis Robertson, is banned from engaging with NBA teams for five years.
Clippers president Laurence Frank will be suspended for six months, while Clippers president of business operations Gillian Zucker is suspended for one year.
Leonard will be fined $700,000, despite pocketing tens of millions from the deal, and not suspended.



	The NBA, who’d hired the law firm Wachtell Lipton to conduct an independent investigation into the Clippers/Leonard saga, found that the Clippers had “committed multiple significant rules violations” and that Leonard, via his uncle, Dennis Robertson, had compelled the Clippers “to assist him in obtaining off-court income opportunities, successfully obtaining those opportunities, and failing to reimburse payments by the Clippers for personal expenses.”

	Leonard released a statement saying, in part, “I accept full responsibility for the lapses in judgment by people within my inner circle,” while NBA commissioner Adam Silver said, “I am deeply disappointed by the flagrant violations of our rules and by the Clippers’ institutional and leadership failures that led to this misconduct. The severity of the penalties reflects the seriousness of the violations.” Ballmer, for his part, released his own statement accusing the NBA of “a heavily biased investigation” and adding they are “exploring every legal remedy to address this gross injustice.”
	

	Variety caught up with Torre to ask him how he feels about everything from the NBA’s ruling (and Leonard’s slap on the wrist) to ESPN and Puck throwing him under the bus.
	
		Do you feel vindicated?	

	Oh man. Hmm … On some level it’s hard to resist the feeling of vindication but truly, my perspective on all of this is that journalism does not exist to be validated by the entity it investigates or by the awards it receives, as much as I welcome and deeply appreciate both. I just think it’s a dangerous game for me to play when the only way you can trust a multipart, monthslong, deeply vetted, obsessively researched series is if the person you investigate has to say, “You know what? This podcaster had a point.” I don’t expect that, but it’s so amazing to have a plot twist in which I get to say any of this.


	
		It says a lot that your work was deeply reported and won a Pulitzer Prize, yet a good portion of the public chose to side with the billionaire and the superstar.	

	It was, for that reason, both vindicating and the opposite. I don’t want that to be the standard. I think it’s good that people have high standards, but the way to assess that is by assessing the work on its own merits. What I’m heartened by is for the people who did take the time to listen — or watch — and really followed the story, there was no ambiguity about what this was.
	
		I wanted to talk to you about ESPN’s report on Aug. 17 that claimed the “NBA has no evidence Ballmer funneled money to Leonard via sponsors.” This is your former employer — that rather coldly showed you the door — releasing a story which seems to be pro-Clippers/Ballmer propaganda and undermined your reporting. I’m sure that made your life hell the last couple of weeks and appears to be the opposite of what journalism should strive to be.	

	My experience with that report was … not great. It was a sign of the power of a mainstream media entity, and the question I always had with this reporting I’ve been doing for a year — which they were not — was why they felt comfortable framing the story that way; and why they never called me before they published it if they were going to frame it that way; and why, after I provided a statement after it published, after being told that they would include it, they never included it? And the statement, to paraphrase it, was simply: “We stand by our reporting. We look forward to the NBA’s ruling. And our investigation continues.”

	What my own reporting suggests is that the Clippers and a crisis PR manager hired by Steve Ballmer were shopping around a story that would be their best chance at telling a version of events that would be helpful to a man — who we now understand, based on the NBA’s investigation, as well as my own — to have repeatedly lied about what really happened. In retrospect, what seems to be the case is that the Clippers fed ESPN information — that the NBA immediately refuted — that deeply resembles the exact press release that the Clippers released almost concurrently with the story. So, it’s not exactly a mystery as to where the information came from, but it is a mystery as to why ESPN presumably consumed at least some of the work we had done over the last year and said to themselves, “This framing of events feels more credible than the former employee we all know who’s provided multiple episodes backed by human sources as well as documentary evidence in which there is no alternate rational explanation for anything that happened other than the thing that he’s been saying for a year.”
	
	
		I also wanted to ask you about the Puck report from Dylan Byers and Peter Hamby which basically accused you of clout-chasing and read like character assassination.	

	This was the work of people who had seemingly no real interest in even consuming the work I’d put out but felt very comfortable attacking my personal standards and credibility as if they had. That felt darkly poetic, in a way, that I would be lectured about proper journalistic standards by apparently a publication that sought to resemble none of them. And personally, I found it confusing and I just think they knew better — or should have — and I don’t think I care to investigate the difference at this point. Whose angle was it? And why did they come up with it? It was either incompetence or malice, and at this point I think there’s an increasingly vanishing distinction. It felt strangely personal. It did.


	
		Well, you did receive public apologies from Mark Cuban and Ty Lawson.	

	And I loved both of those — and the way they came. They’re deeply appreciated.
	
		Let’s talk about the historic penalty against the Clippers that your reporting compelled: A $30 million fine, five first-round draft picks, a yearlong suspension for Steve Ballmer and yet only a $700,000 fine and no suspension for Kawhi Leonard. It seems like Leonard was let off the hook with a tiny fine, compared to the tens of millions he pocketed, and gets to leave the country and be traded to the Toronto Raptors.	

	One of the reasons I think it’s really important not to evaluate journalism based on an outside counsel’s ruling is that sometimes there are negotiations that happen for reasons beyond a reflection of what the truth actually is, and this is a prime case study. Kawhi Leonard, in all the evidence we assembled — and the NBA assembled — was given a slap on the wrist, by that evidentiary standard, but we realize why it happened. According to my reporting, this was a choice that the NBA made in order to take away from the proceedings one of the main options that Steve Ballmer had to make this whole story even messier for the league and his partners, which was arbitration. By giving Kawhi Leonard a slap on the wrist, according to my reporting, the union and Kawhi both agreed to settle; and by settling, they removed arbitration as an option. And so, when Steve Ballmer is punished with this historic punishment, the only move he has is to not take the arbitration — which he mistakenly assumed he still had — but to actually take everybody to court and sue the NBA, the commissioner, Wachtell Lipton, me and whoever he wants. That’s a legal strategy that the league made that is not the same thing as telling you what really happened, and what culpability everybody actually had in terms of what has been alleged.
	
		What did you make of Leonard’s statement which read, in part: “Integrity and respect for this game are fundamental to who I am. I accept full responsibility for the lapses in judgment by people within my inner circle and regret the distraction this situation has caused the fans and my family.” That certainly doesn’t sound like accepting “full responsibility” to me.	

	Kawhi Leonard is an adult. He is a 35-year-old man who was in meetings with all of these teams, and was aware of what his uncle was requesting, and we have documents where his literal signature is in sections that attest to his knowledge and consent to the deals that he is saying he was effectively totally unaware of. By my own collection of documents, it doesn’t make sense to me. But in terms of why he said it, I understand. He’s basically getting to say, “I’m out, this wasn’t great, I regret some things, see you in Toronto.” And the whole story is about a guy that Steve Ballmer wanted so badly that he did not realize the ways in which he, Steve Ballmer, was leaving himself vulnerable to a divergence of self-interest that manifested in the outcome of this entire story.
	



	

					Pablo Torre interviews a guest on “Pablo Torre Finds Out.”
									Getty
	


	
		I know we’ve already discussed this but just so we’re clear: You are not investigating the New York Knicks or Jalen Brunson, correct?	

	They are not a target. At the moment I’m absolutely not focusing on the Knicks or Jalen Brunson.
	
		But you did just tease an investigation into Mark Walter, the owner of the Los Angeles Dodgers, that will be dropping on your pod tomorrow. Walter, of course, is under federal investigation over $21 billion in undisclosed loans made by two insurance companies he owns, and who recently sold the Lakers to Bob Iger and Joshua Kushner, brother to the president’s son-in-law, for $12.5 billion. Can you tell me more about that?	

	Tomorrow — Friday — we have part one of an investigation that also involves federal agencies, also involves the public interest, also involves Hall of Fame basketball players, also involves a team in Los Angeles, also involves a baseball team in Los Angeles, and we’re trying to make something that seems very complicated, once again, something that people realize is not only a lot simpler than they might think, but is also deeply relevant to their interests as the public is concerned. I hope people give it time and sit through it.
	
		How much does this go into Walter’s sale of the Lakers to Iger and Kushner?	

	This is part one, and so certainly part of the impetus was the sale of the Lakers to Bob Iger and Josh Kushner, but we hope to tell the story as the reporting comes in. This is not a one-and-done where everything is in here, but this is our way in. I don’t want to get ahead of ourselves, as it hasn’t come out yet, but I do want to say that we’ve spent months thinking about this and really accelerated the reporting in the last couple of weeks.

title: International Oscar Submissions: Romania, South Korea, Chile, Germany and More Join the List
description:
Sep 3, 2026 4:38pm PT	
	

	
	International Oscar Submissions: Romania, South Korea, Chile, Germany and More Join the List
body:
Sep 3, 2026 4:38pm PT	
	

	
	International Oscar Submissions: Romania, South Korea, Chile, Germany and More Join the List
	



			
			
	
						

									©Netflix/Courtesy Everett Collection
	
					


								
		
				

	The campaigns for the Oscar for international feature film are gaining momentum, with final submissions due by Oct. 1. The Oscars shortlists will be revealed on Dec. 15, with 15 international films selected to be voted on by Academy members in all branches who commit to watch all 15 films. Oscar nominations will be revealed on Jan. 21.

	This year’s entries include titles like Romania’s “Fjord,” which won the Palme d’Or at Cannes; Chile’s “The Meltdown,” which screened in Un Certain Regard; and Germany’s “Everytime,” which won Cannes’ Un Certain Regard prize. 

	France has not yet submitted a film, but faces several disparate choices. 

	Meanwhile, a new Academy rule allows any film that wins the top prize at one of the six biggest festivals — Cannes, Berlin, Venice, Sundance, Busan and Toronto — to be entered in the international feature race even without a national committee’s backing. 


			
			
	Fjord (Romania)
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of Tudor Panduru				
					
				

	“Fjord,” written and directed by Cristian Mungiu, is Romania’s submission for the 2027 Oscars in the best international feature film category, having been unanimously chosen by the country’s selection committee.

	The film premiered in the official competition at the Cannes Film Festival, where it won the Palme d’Or for best film, the FIPRESCI Prize, the Ecumenical Jury Prize, the Prix de la Citoyenneté and the François Chalais Prize.

	Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve star in the lead roles, with cinematography by Tudor Vladimir Panduru, editing by Mircea Olteanu, and production design by Simona Pădurețu.

		
			
			
	Aontas (Ireland)
			
										
					Image Credit: Púca Pictures				
					
				

	“Aontas,” the Irish-language heist thriller from director Damian McCann, has been chosen as Ireland’s entry for the best international feature film category at the 2027 Academy Awards.

	The film was selected by the Irish Film & TV Academy (IFTA) and a committee including “Evil Dead Rise” director Lee Cronin, “Derry Girls” creator Lisa McGee, BAFTA-nominated director Brian Kirk (“Game of Thrones), BAFTA nominated director Kathryn Ferguson (“Nothing Compares”), Emmy-winning actress and filmmaker Aisha Tyler (“Friends”), actress Fionnuala Flaherty (“Kneecap”) and IFTA chief executive Áine Moriarty.

	Told in reverse chronology, “Aontas” follows three unlikely thieves, led by a woman on the verge of a breakdown, who rob a rural Irish bank. Opening in the tragic aftermath of the heist-gone-wrong. What starts as a poorly executed robbery becomes a portrait of a wilful woman trapped in her own past. It stars Carrie Crowley (“The Quiet Girl “), Bríd Brennan, Eva-Jane Gaffney, Seán T. Ó Meallaigh, Marcus Lamb and Art Parkinson.

		
			
			
	The Meltdown (Chile)
			
										
					Image Credit: 'The Meltdown'  Courtesy of Mubi				
					
				

	Chile’s Film Academy has selected “The Meltdown” (“El deshielo”) by Manuela Martelli, her post-Pinochet mystery drama set in an Andes ski resort, to represent the country in the Best International Feature category at the 2027 Academy Awards. Martelli’s follow-up to her acclaimed drama “Chile, 1976” had its world premiere at Cannes’ prominent strand Un Certain Regard this year.

	“The Meltdown” stars Maya O’Rourke – in her film debut – who plays a nine-year-old at her family’s ski resort who witnesses unsettling events that will test her loyalties. Other cast members are Paulina Urrutia, Mauricio Pešutić, Paula Zúñiga, Marcela Salinas and Lautaro Cantillana.

		
			
			
	All of a Sudden (Japan)
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of Neon, Cannes Film Festival				
					
				

	Hamaguchi Ryusuke‘s “All of a Sudden” has been selected as Japan’s entry in the international feature category at the 99th Academy Awards, the Motion Picture Producers Association of Japan (Eiren) has revealed.

	The selection marks the second time a Hamaguchi film has represented Japan in the category, five years after “Drive My Car” won the international feature Oscar and picked up nominations for best picture, director and adapted screenplay at the 94th Academy Awards.

	“All of a Sudden” is a France-Japan co-production made with backing from Germany and Belgium, shot largely in Paris. The film draws on “When Life Suddenly Takes a Turn: Twenty Letters Between a Philosopher With Terminal Cancer and a Medical Anthropologist,” a book of correspondence by Miyano Makiko and Isono Maho. It follows Marie-Lou Fontaine (Virginie Efira), who runs a nursing home outside Paris and pushes to adopt a more dignity-focused model of elderly care, and Morisaki Mari (Okamoto Tao), a Japanese theater director undergoing cancer treatment. Nagatsuka Kyōzō and Kurosaki Kōdai round out the cast.

		
			
			
	Everytime (Germany)
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of The Barricades				
					
				

	Sandra Wollner’s “Everytime” has been selected as Germany’s entry for the Academy Award for best international feature film.

	The film’s synopsis reads as follows: The last photograph Jessie took shows the sun over Berlin. It hangs there as if nothing had happened. But Ella has lost her daughter. What remains is Jessie’s younger sister and a complicated relationship with the boy everyone blames. The unlikely trio ends up on a family holiday that never really existed. Under the shimmering sun of Tenerife, memory and the present become inseparably intertwined. The ghosts are everywhere.

	“Everytime” celebrated its world premiere at the 79th Cannes Film Festival in May. Wollner’s third feature film, for which she also wrote the screenplay, was selected for the Un Certain Regard sidebar where it won the Prix Un Certain Regard, the section’s top award. Cannes was followed by invitations to the Sydney Film Festival and the Karlovy Vary Film Festival, among others. At the Sarajevo Film Festival, “Everytime” was awarded the Heart of Sarajevo Grand Prize. Its North American premiere will follow in September at the Toronto Film Festival. Other festival appearances include the New York Film Festival.

		
			
			
	Becoming Human (Cambodia)
			
										
					Image Credit: Anti-Archive				
					
				

	The Cambodia Oscar Selection Committee (COSC) has selected “Becoming Human,” directed by Polen Ly, as the country’s official submission for the international feature film category at the 99th Academy Awards.

	The film follows Thida, the spirit guardian of an aging cinema slated for demolition, as she weighs the choice of rebirth against her existence as a ghost. Her bond with Hai, a living man she meets along the way, pushes her to confront both her spiritual fate and a country in the midst of sweeping social change.

	“Becoming Human” is Ly’s debut feature. He previously made the short film “Further and Further Away” in 2022 and the documentary “Until the Orchid Blooms,” which premiered at IDFA in 2024 and won the grand prize at the Taiwan International Documentary Festival in 2026. The cast is led by 15-year-old newcomer and dance student Savorn Serak alongside Piseth Chhun, who won the Venice Horizons award for best actor in 2021 for his role in Kavich Neang’s “White Building.”

		
			
			
	Possible Love (South Korea)
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of Netflix, Venice Film Festival				
					
				

	The Korean Film Council (KOFIC) has selected “Possible Love,” directed by Lee Chang-dong, as South Korea‘s official entry for the international feature film category at the 2027 Academy Awards.

	“Possible Love” marks Lee’s first feature in eight years, following “Burning,” “Poetry” and “Secret Sunshine.” The film centers on two married couples whose lives intersect after a funeral: Mi-ok and her laid-off husband Ho-seok (Sul Kyung-gu), who live quietly with their young son Cheol, and Ye-ji, a filmmaker making a documentary about workers who lost their jobs, and her husband Sang-woo (Zo In-sung). When Mi-ok agrees to be filmed by Ye-ji, the two women grow close, while Mi-ok finds herself unsettled by an attraction to Sang-woo. As the two couples’ worlds overlap, cracks begin to surface in both marriages.

	In its evaluation, the committee cited the film’s polished craftsmanship and the clarity of its directorial vision, pointing to the tone and mise-en-scène that sustain a sense of pressure throughout the story. The drama was described as prompting reflection on gentle forms of violence, incomplete freedom and the nature of true happiness, alongside a labor movement sequence that the committee said captured layered social undercurrents.

		
			
			
	Like a Limbless Tree (Turkey)
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy Tekhne Film				
					
				

	“Like a Limbless Tree,” an intimate social drama directed by Tunç Davut, has been selected as Turkey‘s entry for the Academy Award for best international feature film.

	Davut, whose previous works include the 2015 drama “Entanglement and TV series “Serçe” and “Kinali Kuzular,” delves into the fragility of human existence against a backdrop of the theme of immigration in “Like a Limbless Tree.” The film is produced by Istanbul-based Tekhne Film and stars Ali Ipin, Fayyaz Duman and Selen Kurtaran.

	Davut’s drama – which won an award at the Bosphorus Film Festival and was selected for the Antalya Golden Orange Film Festival and the Ankara Film Festival – is about a retired engineer named Refik whose life changes forever after being diagnosed with a terminal disease just as his Syrian caregiver disappears while attempting to flee to Europe, leaving him in charge of her two children.

		
			
			
	How to Divorce During the War (Lithuania)
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of New Europe Film Sales				
					
				

	Andrius Blaževičius’ “How to Divorce During the War” has been selected as Lithuania’s entry for the Academy Award for best international feature film.

	Blaževičius’ third feature won the directing award in the World Cinema Dramatic Competition at the Sundance Film Festival. The film was picked up for theatrical distribution in North America by Zeitgeist Films, in association with Kino Lorber, and will be released on Aug. 21.

	Set in Vilnius in 2022, it’s a story of a high-flying executive Marija, who chooses the worst possible moment for an honest conversation with her husband Vytas about divorcing – just one day before Russia’s invasion of Ukraine goes into full scale. Now the couple must navigate the process of separation as it collides with a refugee and mid-life crisis.

		
	
	


	
		More from Variety

title: Jane Fonda on Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger, Trump and Tech Bros’ Desire for Longevity ‘While They’re Killing the Rest of Us’
description: A feisty Jane Fonda on Thursday spoke out about her opposition to the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger, her aversion to Donald Trump, and the eerie des
body:
A feisty Jane Fonda on Thursday spoke out about her opposition to the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger, her aversion to Donald Trump, and the eerie desire that “tech bros, oligarchs and billionaires” have for longevity, “while they’re killing the rest of us,” as she put it.

	Fonda, 88, took questions from a small group of journalists prior to being honored at the DVF Awards charity gala held on the sidelines of the Venice Film Festival by fashion designer Diane von Furstenberg to honor extraordinary women. The event’s other honorees were the Prime Minister of Barbados Mia Amor Mottley; American photojournalist Lynsey Addario; Kenyan social entrepreneur Wawira Njiru and France’s feminist icon Gisèle Pelicot. 
	

	Though the bulk of the conversation with Fonda was about politics, her activism and the tyranny of tech bros, the two-time Oscar winner also provided an update on her career as an actress.


	“The Correspondent,” Lionsgate’s film adaptation of Virginia Evans’ bestselling novel about a retired lawyer who uses letter-writing to impose order on a complicated world, is now in final stages of pre-production, she said. Fonda hopes cameras will start rolling in January, though “it depends on the director.” And she has other projects percolating: “I just can’t mention them.”

	It’s clear that Fonda is eager to get back in front of the camera.

	“After five years of not working as an actor, I have to confess that — as much as I love the work that I do with my comrades in the movement — I miss the process of becoming somebody else. It is such a thrilling process. I love it. I miss it,” she underlined.
	

	You recently defended Mark Ruffalo’s First Amendment right to speak out about politics and powerful corporations in the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger, which you are opposed to. What is your main concern regarding the prospect of this merger? 

	I am hopeful that we can stop it. They’re carrying so much debt. The Ellisons are carrying so much debt, and it’s being postponed now, so that they have to pay these huge sums. The merger would be terrible for consumers. Prices would go up. Thousands and thousands of people would lose their jobs. And as a creative, the fewer studios there are, the fewer places that we can take our products. We lose bargaining power. Unions lose their power. There’s a very robust and growing movement to stop the mergers. And it, you know, it’s sad for me because I like David Ellison very much. David’s Skydance financed “Grace and Frankie,” my seven-year-long run for Netflix, and I got to know him, and I like him. But that doesn’t change things. This is not a personal thing. This is what it will do to the entertainment industry, which is already suffering terribly.

	How how do you think Ted Turner would have felt about the prospect of Paramount owning CNN?

	Oh, I think he would be terribly upset. He didn’t want to sell back in the day when he sold, and I was still with him then. And I remember all of the big thinkers, you know, the John Malones, the Gordie Crawfords. They were all saying, “You’ve got to do this.” Ted didn’t want to do it, but he did. And now David Zaslav did. Ted would be absolutely heartbroken.

	You stood up for Mark Ruffalo when he was accused of antisemitism. Do you think there’s a blacklist now in Hollywood?

	Absolutely. I mean, this is a tactic that they’re they’re using. Larry Ellison, because he doesn’t like Mark Ruffalo’s position on the merger, accuses him of antisemitism, when he said nothing that that isn’t within his constitutional right to say. It’s a tactic they’re using. He should be ashamed of himself, Larry Ellison. But there’s a lot of support for Mark. A lot of people came forward.

	You started becoming a political activist very young. How important was it for you to take political positions?

	I was 33 years old when I became an activist. And my life before then was so silly. So nothing. So meaningless. And when I became an activist I met entirely different kinds of people. Back in the 1970s, around Vietnam, there was a backlash. But I was part of a movement. I was not alone. This is very important. Mark is part of a movement. He’s not alone. This is a time when we have to stick together. We can’t be alone. They can’t pick us off when we’re alone. 
	

	Has it become harder to speak out about things since Donald Trump’s rise?

	Not for me. No. I’ve had my life. He can do nothing to me. I’m not scared. But that’s not true for everyone, and I understand that. And that’s why I’m encouraging people to join the movement. I created the committee for the First Amendment a year ago, on Oct. 1. It existed in the 1940s and ’50s as a way to confront McCarthy and the witch hunts. My dad was a member. And we have thousands and thousands of members, and we have them come together. We’re building community.

	What happens to normal people who are not you? How do you see the fact that it’s more difficult for them to speak out?

	More and more of them are speaking out. I’ll tell you why. Their whole lives are at risk right now. AI could take away their jobs. And then data centers are being put into their neighborhoods that are destroying [the environment]. There’s been a shift in the U.S. Things are changing. Republicans and Democrats alike are standing there saying, “No. You’re not going to put a data center in my community.” No, you’re not going to put a detention center.” We can see now that MAGA members, even, they’re not liking the fact that their leaders are profiting off misery and cruelty. They don’t like that. They don’t like the chaos that’s happening. They don’t like the way the immigrants are being treated.

	Do you have a presidential candidate that you like for 2028?

	You know, it’s too soon. We don’t know what’s going to happen. I can tell you though. I’m looking at Jon Ossoff. Aside from the presidential race aside, there are some young politicians I like. Justin Pearson [the Tennessee State Representative who is running for Congress in November], for example. There’s a woman, Peggy Flanagan, [Lieutenant Governor of Minnesota since 2019 who is a Democrat running for the United States Senate in 2026]. She’s an Indigenous woman, Ojibwe from Minnesota. She’s going to get into the Senate. I mean, imagine if we had senators who thought, “Hmm, the decision I’m going to make now. How is it going to affect people seven generations from now?”

	Within the global elites, longevity seems to be all the rage. What are your thoughts on that?

	They want to live forever, while they’re killing the rest of us. There’s two things: Most of these guys, these tech bros and these oligarchs and billionaires, they feel that the laws that the rest of us live by don’t matter to them, including the laws of physics. Natural laws. They’re going to live forever. That’s one [thing]. The other is that because these [ageless] guys can’t have babies, they’ll create robots. That’ll be their babies. And they’ll just turn the rest of us into tradwives, who have a lot of babies too. Then they’ll take away the vote. Can you believe it? And we’re not going to stand for it. They’re not going to win, because we’re not going to stand for it. The big problem is — and this has never happened in the history of humankind — if this was happening at any other time, you could say: “We’re going to win, in the end.” But because of the climate crisis, we don’t have that much time. You know, there’s a point where if it gets too hot. Then there’s no going back.
	

	This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.



	

									Stafano Trovati|SGPC/Courtesy DvF

title: Miley Cyrus Leads a Steamy Dance Floor Revolution With New Single and Video for ‘Bass Persuades’
description: Miley Cyrus is setting off her new era with the release of the single and video for “Bass Persuades,” the title track off her upcoming 10th album.
body:
Miley Cyrus is setting off her new era with the release of the single and video for “Bass Persuades,” the title track off her upcoming 10th album.

	“Bass Persuades” goes full dance-pop with tinges of ’80s synths and a spoken-word first verse that recalls the deadpan delivery of Lady Gaga on “Poker Face.” “Step into the scene you won’t catch an eye / Walk into the party like the party is mine,” she commands. “Paving over pastures ’cause horses are gone / Forgetting there’s a world when this is record is on.” The record decidedly guns for the dance floor, not far off from the spirit of “Something Beautiful” cuts “Walk of Fame” or “Every Girl You’ve Ever Loved.”
	

	Cyrus also released the video for the song, which can be viewed below:




	Cyrus recently announced that “Bass Persuades” will be released on September 18 via Atlantic Records. This marks her first project as part of her recently minted deal Atlantic, which comes after two albums on Columbia including “Endless Summer Vacation” and “Something Beautiful.”

	For “Bass Persuades,” which features 10 tracks, Cyrus appeared to drop her last name to go mononomously this era. Earlier this week, she revealed the title and cover art for the album, explaining her mission statement on social media: “Music takes hold of us. We feel it, sing it, sometimes dance to it, let it out and carry on. It is powerful, vulnerable, sweet and strong,” she wrote. “Heart full, heartache, every part of life in between. That’s what the title means to me. Thank you for being a part of making my wildest dreams come true. I sincerely hope you love this album.”
	

	Cyrus also announced her grand return to the stage with a pair of shows at Los Angeles’ Hollywood Bowl on October 16 and 18. The gigs will feature support from Model/Actriz, who appears on “Bass Persuades,” and the flier suggests that Cyrus will be performing the album in full.

schema.headline: Miley Cyrus Leads a Steamy Dance Floor Revolution With New Single and Video for ‘Bass Persuades’

title: Late NASCAR Star Greg Biffle’s Ex-Wife Seeking $10 Million from Estate Over Daughter’s Death in Plane Crash

Late NASCAR Driver Greg Biffle
                          Ex-Wife Wants $10 Million From Estate
body:
Late NASCAR Driver Greg Biffle
                          Ex-Wife Wants $10 Million From Estate
                          After Daughter Dies In Tragic Plane Crash
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              
                September 3, 2026
                
                            12:58 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  September 3, 2026
                                1:43 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Late NASCAR star Greg Biffle’s ex-wife, Nicole Biffle, wants his estate to pay hefty damages after she lost her daughter in a plane crash ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            According to court docs obtained by TMZ, Nicole filed a claim against the late driver's estate in the amount of $10 million for Emma Biffle’s death on December 18, 2025, in North Carolina.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Emma was on board the fatal flight with Greg, and Nicole has already filed a wrongful death action against the estate.  In the new docs, Nicole is asking for an order preventing the estate from making any further distributions to ensure there is money left over to pay her claim and similar ones filed by the estates of others who died in the crash.
      

            As TMZ previously reported, Greg’s estate is facing three separate wrongful death lawsuits. The first two suits were filed by Dennis Dutton and his son Jack, who were on board the plane. The lawsuits filed on their behalf are seeking a total of $30 million.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            The plane crashed minutes after the jet took off from Statesville Regional Airport.
      
    
            Nicole claimed her daughter was sick on the day the jet took off and asked not to take the trip ... but claims Greg was "insistent that Emma accompany him." She claims Greg and others were negligent, which caused the crash.
      
    
            Now, the estate is facing $40 million in claims over the fatal crash.

title: 'Wheel of Fortune's' Jim Thornton: See Pedophilia Chatroom Photos Behind Suspension

                          See Pedophilia Chatroom Pics That Led to S
body:
'Wheel of Fortune's' Jim Thornton
                          See Pedophilia Chatroom Pics That Led to Suspension
                      
              
    
            These are the photos that got "Wheel of Fortune" announcer Jim Thornton suspended by the show and grilled by law enforcement.
      
    
            Thornton was on an American Airlines flight back in May from Charlotte to L.A. ... when a passenger eyed his laptop and saw him in a disturbing chatroom. The passenger tells TMZ, she saw images and texts that made it appear it was a chatroom for pedophiles.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            One of the messages she saw said, "Couple of cute boys and a hot little girl." Another read, "All-you-can-eat Boyfett." referring to a restaurant where they could find underage kids.
      

            And there's another message references "CP," which the passenger believed stood for child porn.
      
    
            As a result, the passenger notified a flight attendant and shared these photos with the crew. We're told the captain then notified authorities, and law enforcement met the plane when it landed at LAX.
      
    
            We're told authorities questioned Thornton and he was then free to leave.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Jim’s lawyer, Allison Hart, tells TMZ, Thornton had “become active in suicide-prevention advocacy since losing a close family member to suicide two years ago, and he has spent time visiting chat rooms offering support to individuals suffering from suicidal ideation.”
      
    
            The "Wheel of Fortune" announcer’s attorney said he often visited a suicide prevention website named 988lifeline.org and its chat forum, chat.988lifeline.org. 
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Jim claims he was sent a link to a different chatroom, lifeline.chat, from an acquaintance at the suicide prevention group. Lifeline.chat is for people with pedophilic thoughts. 
      
    
            The announcer claims he left the chatroom once he found out what it was, although from the timestamps it appears Thornton was in the room for at least 57 minutes.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            His lawyer added that website lifeline.chat is “not unlawful, there is no unlawful child pornography or other pedophilic content, and my client never viewed, downloaded or consumed any child pornography whether on that commercial flight in May or at any other time.” 
      
    
            Jim’s lawyer said their client was never arrested or charged with a crime. His lawyer claimed law enforcement spoke to Jim once he landed and determined no crime had occurred. “In short, my client did nothing wrong,” she said.

title: Musician, Pregnant Wife and 3-Year-Old Daughter Shot to Death in Mexico
description:
Mexican Musician
                          Executed With Pregnant Wife And 3-Year-Old Daughter ..
body:
Mexican Musician
                          Executed With Pregnant Wife And 3-Year-Old Daughter ...
                          6-Year-Old Boy Spared
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              
                September 3, 2026
                
                            6:39 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  September 3, 2026
                                4:59 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A rock musician was shot to death and found Tuesday in Mexico, along with most of his family, including his pregnant wife and 3-year-old daughter, according to CNN.
      
    
            The news outlet reported that Jonathan Meléndez, a 35-year-old keyboardist for indie rock band Camilo Séptimo, was gunned down with his wife, Ana Paula, 35, who was 4 months pregnant, inside their upscale home in Mexico City.
      
    
            Melendez's young daughter was also fatally shot along with her 21-year-old nanny, CNN said, citing the Mexico Attorney General’s Office.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The Attorney General said 3 of the victims -- including the daughter -- were shot in the backs of their heads, while a fourth victim was shot in the back.
      
    
            The AG also said 2 victims had their hands tied, and the family dog was found dead with its legs bound. A 6-year-old boy was found unharmed at the scene.
      
    
            Police arrested two men in connection with the murders -- and prosecutors say one suspect used his relationship with one of the victims to enter the home.

body:
Sydney Sweeney & Scooter Braun
                          That's Amore ...
                          Gondola Ride in Venice!!!
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Sydney Sweeney's been spending more time with Scooter Braun's kids in recent weeks ... but it looks like the pair are on a romantic adventure for 2 -- jetting off to Venice to flaunt their amore.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The actress and her music-mogul man were spotted in the Floating City on Thursday ... sitting back and relaxing as a gondolier paddled them around the town.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The couple dressed casually in matching white outfits ... though Scooter added splashes of blue with his shorts and backwards baseball cap.
      

            Sydney and Scooter were hanging all over each other throughout the day ... hands clasped tightly and grins on their faces.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            It's been a busy week for the duo ... who were actually just in Los Angeles on Tuesday -- grabbing smoothies with two of Scooter's kids.
      
    
            This was the second time we'd seen them with the kids in recent days ... after first spotting them getting off a private jet in Los Angeles as a quintet.
      
    
            Quality time as a group can be good ... but we'd guess these two think their time alone is molto bene!
